original_question: For the shifted moment Mk(T, alpha) = integral from 0 to T of the product over i of |zeta(1/2 + t + alpha_i)|^(2k_i) dt, Chandee proved an upper bound of the shape Mk(T, alpha) <<_{k,epsilon} T (log T)^(k_1^2 + ... + k_m^2 + epsilon) times the product over i < j of min{1/|alpha_i - alpha_j|, log T}^{2 k_i k_j}, under the stated hypotheses on the shifts alpha_i(T). Use Harper’s method to remove the epsilon from this bound.
target_in_paper: Problem (5) in the section Problems → Moments of the Riemann zeta function: improve Chandee’s [14, Theorem 1.2] by using Harper’s method to remove the ε from the quoted upper bound for the general shifted moment M_k(T, α). ([personal.math.ubc.ca](https://personal.math.ubc.ca/~gerg/papers/downloads/MLPL.pdf))
correct_elements: Your draft has the right target, the right quantity M_k(T, α), the right bound-shape, and the right methodological goal: it is indeed the Problem (5) entry asking for Chandee’s shifted-moment upper bound to be sharpened by removing the ε via Harper’s method. ([personal.math.ubc.ca](https://personal.math.ubc.ca/~gerg/papers/downloads/MLPL.pdf))
missing_details: The paper’s formula uses ζ(1/2 + i(t + α_i)), so the factor i in the zeta argument is essential; your draft writes 1/2 + t + α_i instead. ([personal.math.ubc.ca](https://personal.math.ubc.ca/~gerg/papers/downloads/MLPL.pdf))

The paper makes m implicit but arbitrary: one should quantify that m ≥ 1 is fixed and that k = (k_1, …, k_m) with each k_i > 0. ([personal.math.ubc.ca](https://personal.math.ubc.ca/~gerg/papers/downloads/MLPL.pdf))

The shift hypotheses must be spelled out explicitly: α_i = α_i(T) are real-valued functions of T with α_i = o(T). ([personal.math.ubc.ca](https://personal.math.ubc.ca/~gerg/papers/downloads/MLPL.pdf))
For each i, the limit lim_{T→∞} α_i log T must exist or equal ±∞. ([personal.math.ubc.ca](https://personal.math.ubc.ca/~gerg/papers/downloads/MLPL.pdf))
For each i ≠ j, the limit lim_{T→∞} (α_i − α_j) log T must exist or equal ±∞. ([personal.math.ubc.ca](https://personal.math.ubc.ca/~gerg/papers/downloads/MLPL.pdf))
The shifts are required to be pairwise distinct: α_i ≠ α_j for i ≠ j. ([personal.math.ubc.ca](https://personal.math.ubc.ca/~gerg/papers/downloads/MLPL.pdf))

The paper also assumes bounded pairwise gaps α_i − α_j = O(1) for i ≠ j; your draft only says 'under the stated hypotheses' and so is not stand-alone. ([personal.math.ubc.ca](https://personal.math.ubc.ca/~gerg/papers/downloads/MLPL.pdf))
The estimate is RH-conditional and only asserted for sufficiently large T; both quantifiers should be stated. ([personal.math.ubc.ca](https://personal.math.ubc.ca/~gerg/papers/downloads/MLPL.pdf))

To make the sharpened claim precise, the post-improvement bound should be written with an implied constant depending only on k, i.e. ≪_k rather than ≪_{k,ε}. ([personal.math.ubc.ca](https://personal.math.ubc.ca/~gerg/papers/downloads/MLPL.pdf))

For fidelity to the paper’s local context, it is worth noting that the paper frames this as the general-m problem beyond the already-treated special case m = 2 and k_1 = k_2. ([personal.math.ubc.ca](https://personal.math.ubc.ca/~gerg/papers/downloads/MLPL.pdf))
refined_question:
Assuming the Riemann Hypothesis, let m ≥ 1 be fixed, let k = (k_1, …, k_m) with k_i > 0, and let α = (α_1, …, α_m) where each α_i = α_i(T) is a real-valued function satisfying α_i = o(T), such that each limit lim_{T→∞} α_i log T and each limit lim_{T→∞}(α_i − α_j) log T exists in ℝ ∪ {±∞}, and for i ≠ j one has α_i ≠ α_j and α_i − α_j = O(1). Define
M_k(T, α) = ∫_0^T ∏_{i=1}^m |ζ(1/2 + i(t + α_i))|^(2k_i) dt.
Use Harper’s method to prove that, for all sufficiently large T,
M_k(T, α) ≪_k T (log T)^(k_1^2 + ··· + k_m^2) ∏_{1≤i<j≤m} (min{1/|α_i − α_j|, log T})^(2k_i k_j),
thereby removing the ε from Chandee’s quoted bound while keeping the same hypotheses on the shifts. ([personal.math.ubc.ca](https://personal.math.ubc.ca/~gerg/papers/downloads/MLPL.pdf))
justification: The draft is not aiming at a conjecture or theorem numbered in the introductory literature cited by the paper; it is aiming directly at Problem (5) of arXiv:2405.17800. That problem reproduces the relevant Chandee theorem, defines the shifted moment M_k(T, α), and then asks: 'Use Harper’s method [40] to remove the ε,' with the added scope note that the two-shift equal-exponent case had already been treated in [60]. The same problem entry also records that Michael Curran [25] solved it, so within the paper this is a historically open problem rather than a presently open one. ([personal.math.ubc.ca](https://personal.math.ubc.ca/~gerg/papers/downloads/MLPL.pdf))
